extracted.subtask_description: Practical and ethical guidelines for crafting personal memoirs, covering voice, structure, factual accuracy, dealing with real people, scenecraft, and revision strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize accuracy and honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine memoirists prioritize accuracy; memoirs should represent the author's truths as faithfully as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr contrasts honest memoirists (e.g., Hilary Mantel, David Carr) with deceitful ones and warns that public validation can overshadow truth (case of Binjamin Wilkomirski). Nurture a discerning readership that values honesty amid deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deceit, sensationalism, and exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not distort life events for fame or dramatic effect; sensationalism can dishonor authentic experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include James Frey and Greg Mortenson. Karr stresses that the most dramatic events don't necessarily make the best memoirs and that exaggeration undermines relatability; write with emotional honesty and normalize the strange rather than sensationalize it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center interiority and the 'inner enemy' (inner conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: A compelling memoir revolves around the author's inner conflicts—the 'inner enemy'—which propel narrative and reader connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interiority enables readers to connect deeply via psychic struggles; memoirists should depict awakening moments of consciousness, fragmented memories that form identity, and the evolution from a split self toward self-discovery (examples: Nabokov, Conroy, Crews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability as narrative resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Vulnerability deepens emotional resonance and allows readers to connect with the author's humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr cites Elie Wiesel's admission of personal guilt as enhancing connection. Embracing vulnerability may be painful but enriches the narrative's emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and preserve an authentic voice; avoid fake voices and pretense
rubrics_metrics.description: Find and use a voice true to your experience rather than adopting polished or pretentious personas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr describes her own shift from hiding behind polished personas to embracing the language of her upbringing. Avoid posturing; recognize when you 'want to sound more intellectual' and instead write from genuine emotional expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for writing about real people (dealing with beloveds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical ethical guidelines for portraying family, friends, and other real people in memoirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr's enumerated rules include: (1) notify subjects in advance about sensitive content; (2) avoid showing pages mid-process; (3) approach writing about disliked individuals with an attitude of love; (4) speculate on others’ feelings while focusing on personal experience; (5) acknowledge opposing views without feeling compelled to fully represent them; (6) avoid dehumanizing language—provide detailed descriptions instead; (7) allow subjects to choose their own pseudonyms; (8) remain open to being incorrect about your recollections; (9) consider reading sensitive material in the presence of those affected; (10) remove any content flatly denied by subjects; (11) clarify the subjectivity of your perspective to honor differing opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed facts and background information within vivid scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts and data should be woven into evocative scenes rather than presented as dry exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skillful writers make facts almost unnoticeable by embedding them in memories or tangible experiences. Use anecdote and sensory detail (smell, sound, imagery) to convey character and context (examples: Frank McCourt, George Orwell).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order information strategically; use structure to set emotional stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with an emotional flash-forward and then proceed linearly; use structure to establish stakes and organize complex personal histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr's preferred book structure starts with an emotional flash-forward before recounting events in order. Imagine telling the story to a friend to discover logical flow. Distinguish the 'capital-S Story' (overarching narrative) from smaller anecdotes that cumulatively reveal it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and confront blind spots and false selves
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must recognize tendencies to self-deceive or present flattering false selves and actively seek emotional realities beneath those masks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Real You' emerges when false selves are discarded. Be vigilant about blind spots, accept that memory is fluid, and actively search for key scenes that reveal emotional truth; writers often discover crucial scenes late in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the narrator undergoes transformation (show inner life)
rubrics_metrics.description: A memoir should trace change in the narrator's inner life—psychological growth, realization, or transformation across the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoirs fail when narrators don't undergo transformation or when inner life is not convincingly depicted. In an age of visual media, writers must excel at conveying interior change that film often leaves out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft emotionally resonant scenes with vivid sensory detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Use rich sensory specifics to turn dry information into engaging, emotionally charged moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: supply smells, sounds, and precise behavioral detail to deepen reader understanding (e.g., a drive with a parent becomes resonant through sensory detail). Good scenes evoke genuine feeling rather than merely report facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write with clarity, brevity, and disciplined prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow principles of clear, vigorous, and concise writing as foundational skills for memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoke George Orwell's advice: aim for clarity and brevity. Self-discipline is necessary to endure uncertainty and revise toward cleaner prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble core requirements before sustained work (initial requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have essentials ready—vivid memories, passion to tell, necessary introductory information, and endurance for blank periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr lists 'crisp memories,' 'passion to tell,' 'introductory information,' and 'endurance in blankness' as prerequisites to begin a memoir in earnest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist items for a viable memoir
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete checklist elements that collectively support a strong memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key checklist items include: create a tangible physical setting rich in sensory detail; develop a story that reveals environment and showcases strengths; infuse emotional conflict in present self or backstory; highlight emotional stakes and underlying struggles; engage in introspection and display revelations; navigate between past and present perspectives; build rapport with readers about truth and memory; emphasize survival (not prolonged suffering) and consider using humor; ensure authenticity and avoid exaggeration; cultivate empathy for characters and recognize their motivations and backstories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize survival and empathy rather than sustained bitterness
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame narratives around survival and human complexity; avoid dwelling solely on bitterness or revenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karr suggests memoirs should emphasize endurance and recovery, possibly using humor, and cultivate empathy for all characters rather than presenting one-dimensional opponents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'old-school' craft practices to stay productive
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ practical habits and tools to maintain momentum and deepen craft when stalled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies include: keeping a commonplace book of admired lines; writing reviews or critiques to build discipline; maintaining a reading journal with one-page reviews and quotes; using index card quotes with sources; memorizing poems to learn economy; and writing longhand letters to characters or historical figures to explore voice and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision is essential—balance generative and editorial selves
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality memoirs arise from extensive revision; writers must foster both generative creativity and ruthless editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision is often painful but necessary; historical reading raises standards; develop an inner editor alongside the generative self; collaborate with peers/workshops for outside perspective; treat mistakes as opportunities and approach revision with curiosity.
